messages:
Maya (PM): Quick post-launch prio sync — we need to decide which of the top 5 issues go into next sprint. TL;DR: one regression reported by Acme (high p99), two UX polish asks, one small perf bug, one feature request from EAP.

Oleg (Eng): Can we get telemetry on % of users hitting the regression? If small segment, maybe patch only for customers.

Maya (PM): Acme accounts for ~30% of failing traces, p99 spike ~400ms. Link: https://redwood.atlassian/PLAT-1234 :face_with_head_bandage:

Tara (UX): My vote: regressions with customer outage = ship patch into hotfix sprint. UX polish can wait.

Kevin (ProdOps): Agree. Also propose we use these heuristics: 1) customer outage/regression; 2) security/compliance; 3) frequency/impact; 4) effort <= 3 dev-days can be fast-tracked; 5) strategic customer asks for committed customers.

Sam (SRE): +1. Can we add "regression risk" — i.e., how likely a change will cause new regressions? Use canary for risky fixes.

Maya (PM): Proposed plan: next sprint reserve 2 dev-days for urgent patch, 3 dev-days for high-impact polish, remainder for enhancements. Canary plan: 10% traffic + feature flag.

Oleg (Eng): I'll owner the regression fix. ETA 3 days incl. canary. I'll open PR and tag @Maya for verification.

Tara (UX): I'll move the 2 polish tickets to sprint backlog and add acceptance criteria.

Maya (PM): OK — I'll update the roadmap doc and put a "prio heuristics" section. Anyone opposed? :thumbsup: for yes

Kevin (ProdOps): :thumbsup:

Sam (SRE): :thumbsup:

Maya (PM): Great — action items: Oleg (regression fix) / Tara (polish) / Maya (roadmap + comms). We'll reevaluate end of week. Thanks!
